p1.original: 我们已经了解如何使用非暴力沟通来发展友谊，促进家庭和睦，改善工作交流以及推动政治和解。然而，非暴力沟通最重要的应用也许在于——爱护自己。
p1.en: We have learned how to use Nonviolent Communication to develop friendship, foster family harmony, improve work exchanges and promote political reconciliation. However, the most important application of Nonviolent Communication may be — caring for oneself.

p2.en: Let the flowers of life bloom.

p3.original: 在赫布·加德纳（Herb Gardner）编写的《一千个小丑》一剧中，主人公拒绝将他12岁的外甥交给儿童福利院。他郑重地说道：“我希望他准确无误地知道他是多么特殊的生命，要不，他在成长的过程中将会忽视这一点。我希望他保持清醒，并看到各种奇妙的可能。我希望他知道，一旦有机会，排除万难给世界一点触动是值得的。我还希望他知道为什么他是一个人，而不是一张椅子。”
p3.en: In Herb Gardner, a play " 1,000 Joker ", the master refused to hand over his 12-year-old nephew to a child welfare home. He solemnly said: “I hope he knows exactly how special his life is, and otherwise he will lose sight of it as he grows up. I want him to stay awake and see all the wonderful possibilities. I hope he knows that, once he has the opportunity, it is worth a little touch of the world to overcome all odds. I also wish he knew why he was alone, not a chair.

p4.original: 然而，一旦负面的自我评价使我们看不到生命的美，我们就会忘记自己是“特殊的生命”，而把自己当作一张椅子。如果我们习惯于将自己视为工具——充满各种缺陷的工具，自我憎恨还令人奇怪吗？
p4.en: However, once negative self-evaluation has made us lose sight of the beauty of life, we forget that we are “special lives” and treat ourselves as a chair. Is self-hatred strange if we are used to view ourselves as a tool — a tool full of flaws?

p5.original: 如何培养对自己的爱呢？转变自我评价的方式是一个重要方面。既然希望自己所做的任何事情都是有益的，那么，自我评价的方式就要有助于学习，使我们的选择符合生命的需要。然而，不幸的是，我们的自我评价方式往往导致自我憎恨，而无助于学习。
p5.en: How can you develop love for yourself? The shift in approach to self-evaluation is an important aspect. Since anything that is desired to be done by ourselves is useful, self-evaluation must be done in a way that helps to learn and that allows our choices to be adapted to the needs of life. Unfortunately, however, our approach to self-evaluation often leads to self-hatred rather than to learning.

p7.original: 在一个研讨班中，我请参加者回忆近期他们做后就感到后悔的一件事情。接着，我提醒他们特别注意，他们认为自己做错事后，会和自己说什么。比较典型的话有：“笨蛋！”“这种蠢事你也干得出！”“你有毛病？”“你总是把事情搞得一团糟！”“真自私！”
p7.en: In a workshop, I asked participants to recall something that they had regretted since they had done recently. I then reminded them of what they would say to themselves when they thought they had done wrong. And the more typical thing is, "Idiot!" "You can do such stupid things! "What's wrong with you?" "You're always making a mess of things." "It's selfish.

p8.original: 他们的自责意味着：他们认为自己所做的事情是错的或不好的，他们应当为此感到痛苦。然而，可悲的是，许多人陷于自我憎恨之中，而无法从失误中获益——失误揭示我们的局限性，并引导我们的成长。
p8.en: Their own blame means that they feel that what they do is wrong or bad, and that they should suffer for it. Tragically, however, many are trapped in self-hatred and unable to benefit from mistakes — failures that reveal our limitations and lead us to growth.

p9.original: 即使我们有时通过严厉的自责“得到了教训”，我也会担心这种变化和学习的驱动力。我希望，我们的改变是出于对生命的爱，而不是出于羞愧或内疚这些具有负面影响的心理。
p9.en: Even though we sometimes “required lessons” through harsh self-recusing, I am concerned about the driving forces of this change and learning. I hope that our change is out of love for life, not out of shame or guilt, which has a negative impact.

p10.original: 如果自我评价使我们羞愧并改变行为，我们也就允许自我憎恨来引导自己的成长和学习。羞愧是自我憎恨的一种形式，出于羞愧的行为不是自由而快乐的行为。即使我们试图更加友善和体贴，一旦人们意识到我们行为背后的羞愧或内疚，他们对这些行为的欣赏也就比不上那些只是出于爱的行为。
p10.en: If self-evaluation shames us and changes our behaviour, we also allow self-hate to guide our own growth and learning. Humiliation is a form of self-hatred, and acts of shame are not acts of freedom and happiness. Even if we try to be more friendly and considerate, when people realize the shame or guilt behind our actions, they will not appreciate them as much as they do because of love.

p11.original: 在我们的语言中，有一个词极易引起羞愧和内疚。我们经常使用它来打击自己。它在我们的意识中是如此根深蒂固，以致许多人无法想象，没有它生活将如何继续。这个词就是“应该”，也就是“我应该早点知道”或“我不应该做那件事情”中的“应该”。如果我们认为自己“应该”怎么样，在大多数的情况下，我们也就封闭了自我。因为“应该”意味着我们别无选择。这使我们感到无奈和沮丧。同时，又心有不甘，不愿屈服。
p11.en: In our language, there is a word that is extremely prone to shame and guilt. We often use it against ourselves. It is so deep-rooted in our consciousness that many people cannot imagine how life would continue without it. The word is “should”, that is, “I should have known earlier” or “I should have done something”. If we think we should, in most cases, shut ourselves down. Because “should” means that we have no choice. That makes us feel helpless and frustrated. At the same time, there is a reluctance to submit.

p12.original: 除了“应该”这个词，我们还用别的方式教训自己，例如：“我真受不了自己现在这个样子。我必须改改了。”想一想那些强迫自己的人。他们中有的人说：“我真的应该戒烟了。”另一些人说：“我必须加强锻炼。”他们不断地说他们“必须”做什么，与此同时，又不停地找借口不那么做，因为没有人想成为奴隶。当然，我们也不是命中注定要去服从“应该”或“不得不”的指挥，不论它们是来自外部，还是来自我们自身。一旦顺从了这些命令，生活也就会失去乐趣。
p12.en: In addition to the word “should”, we have taught ourselves in other ways, for example: “I can't stand the way I am now. I have to change it. "Think about those who force themselves. One of them said, "I really should quit smoking. Others said, "I need to strengthen my exercise. “They keep saying what they “must” do, and at the same time they keep looking for excuses not to do so, because no one wants to be a slave. Of course, we are not destined to be subject to “should” or “must” command, whether they come from outside or from ourselves. Once these orders are followed, life loses its fun.

p14.original: 经常责备自己、强迫自己将使我们“更像椅子而不像人”。非暴力沟通认为，对他人的指责反映了我们遇到了挫折——他人的行为不符合我们的需要。如果我们指责的那个人恰好是我们自己，那么，言下之意是：“我的行为不符合我的需要。”我相信，如果我们专注于需要是否得到满足以及得到怎样的满足，我们就更有可能从自我评价中获益。
p14.en: Often blaming ourselves and forcing ourselves will make us “more like chairs than people”. Nonviolent Communication suggests that the accusations against others reflect the setbacks we have encountered — the behaviour of others that is not in keeping with our needs. If the person we blame happens to be ourselves, then the implication is: “My actions do not fit my needs. “I believe that if we focus on whether and how needs are met, we are more likely to benefit from self-evaluation.

p15.original: 一旦发现自己正在做无益的事情，我们的挑战是如何对需要和价值观保持清醒的认识，以使我们的转变：
p15.en: Once we find ourselves doing something that is not useful, the challenge is to keep our needs and values in perspective so that we can change:

p16.en: (1) It is in line with our wishes;

p17.original: （2）出于对自己的尊重和爱护，而不是出于自我憎恨、内疚或羞愧。
p17.en: (2) Out of respect and love for oneself, not out of self-hatred, guilt or shame.

p19.original: 我们成长在学校教育和社会化的影响中，对于大多数的人来说，培养自己在各种情境中都专注于生命的需要及价值观，也许已经太迟了。然而，既然我们可以用心体会他人的评论所反映的需要，我们一样可以了解自责所反映的需要。
p19.en: It may be too late for most of us to grow up in the impact of school education and socialization to be able to focus on the needs and values of life in all situations. However, since we can understand the needs reflected in others ' comments, we can understand the needs reflected in self-responsibility as well.

p20.original: 例如，如果发现我们痛骂自己：“你看你，又把事情搞砸了！”我们马上就可以问：“我什么样的需要没有得到满足？”一旦意识到自己尚未满足的需要——很可能是多个层面的需要，我们的身心状态就会发生明显的变化。我们不再感到羞愧、内疚和沮丧，而开始体会到别的情感。不论它们是忧愁、失望、恐惧、悲伤、挫折感或别的——其目的都是推动我们去满足需要和追逐梦想。
p20.en: For example, if we find ourselves scolded: "Look at you, and you screw up again! "What kind of need I have not met?" “When we realize that our unmet needs — most likely at multiple levels — are met, our physical and mental state will change dramatically. Instead of feeling shame, guilt and frustration, we are beginning to feel other feelings. Whether they are sorrow, despair, fear, sorrow, frustration or something — the purpose is to drive us to meet our needs and pursue our dreams.

p21.original: 非暴力沟通鼓励我们直面人生的苦难：在遇到挫折时，充分体会人生的悲哀和内心的渴望。是的，感到遗憾是难免的。但它能帮助我们从经历中学习，而无须责备自己。我们意识到过去的行为违背了自己的需要及价值观，并允许这种觉察引发的情感充分流淌。一旦专注于尚未满足的需要，我们就会考虑如何满足它。反之，如果用苛刻的语言指责自己，我们不仅难以找到解决办法，而且容易陷于自我惩罚的痛苦中。
p21.en: Nonviolent Communication encourages us to confront the suffering of our lives: to fully appreciate the sadness of our lives and the aspirations of our hearts when we encounter setbacks. Yes, regret is inevitable. But it can help us learn from experience without blaming ourselves. We are aware that the past has acted against our own needs and values, and allow the emotions generated by this perception to flow to the full. Once we focus on the needs that remain unmet, we will consider how to meet them. On the contrary, if we accuse ourselves in harsh language, we not only have difficulty finding solutions, but we are also vulnerable to the pain of self-punitiveness.

p23.original: 接着，我们试图理解自己过去的所作所为。我们问自己：“我做那件事情是为了满足什么需要？”我相信，人的行为总是服务于自身的需要及价值观——不论它是否能够实现目的，也不论我们事后是感到庆幸还是遗憾。
p23.en: Then we tried to understand what we had done in the past. We asked ourselves, “What need do I have to do that? “I believe that human beings always act in the service of their own needs and values — whether or not they achieve their purpose, whether or not we are happy or sorry afterwards.

p24.original: 通过聆听自己的心声，我们就能发现心灵深处的需要。此时，我们就可以原谅自己。我们意识到，尽管过去的选择并不理想，但它也是为了实现内心的渴望。
p24.en: By listening to our hearts, we can discover the needs of our hearts. At this point, we can forgive ourselves. We are aware that, while the options of the past are not ideal, they are also meant to fulfil the aspirations of the heart.

p25.original: 爱惜自己的关键之一是同时包容那两个不同的“我”：一方面包容对过去的某种行为感到后悔的“我”，另一方面包容采取那种行为的“我”。非暴力沟通的忧伤及自我宽恕为个人的学习和成长创造了条件。只要对自己的需要保持清醒的认识，我们就能建设性地满足它们。
p25.en: One of the keys to loving one's own is to accommodate the two different “I”s: “I”s, on the one hand, and “I”s, on the other hand, who have expressed regret for something of the past, on the other. The sadness of Nonviolent Communication and self-excuse create the conditions for individual learning and growth. As long as we remain conscious of their needs, we can meet them constructively.

p26.original: 外衣染上墨水带来的启发
p26.en: The ink on the coat is the inspiration.

p27.original: 我想通过个人经历来说明非暴力沟通的忧伤及自我宽恕。在一个研讨班开始前的一天，我买了一套浅灰色的夏季外衣。这个研讨班很重要，出席的人很多。在结束时，许多人围着我询问地址及其他信息，并请我签名。为了赶下一场会面，我匆忙地回答问题，并紧张地签字和留言。当我飞快地冲出门时，我将笔放入了新外套的口袋。我居然忘了戴笔帽！等到了外面，我吓了一跳——那件雅致的浅灰色外套已染上了墨水！
p27.en: I would like to illustrate through my personal experience the sadness of Nonviolent Communication and my own forgiveness. On the day before the start of a seminar, I bought a gray summer coat. This seminar was important, and it was attended by a lot of people. At the end, many people surrounded me with questions about the address and other information and asked me to sign them. In an effort to rush the next meeting, I answered the questions in a hasty manner and signed and left a message with tension. When I ran out of the house, I put my pen in the pocket of my new coat. I forgot my pen hat! When I got outside, I was surprised -- that elegant gray coat was ink-drinked!

p28.original: 有二十分钟的时间，我不停地训斥自己：“你怎么可以这么粗心？这么愚蠢的错误！”我刚损失了一套崭新的外衣，如果我在生活中需要得到体谅，那么，此刻正是时候。可是，我却是在训斥自己，这简直糟透了。
p28.en: I've had 20 minutes, and I've been scolding myself, "How can you be so careless? Such a stupid mistake! "I just lost a brand-new jacket, and if I need to be understanding in my life, then this is the right time. But I'm scolding myself, and that's terrible.

p29.original: 幸运的是，二十分钟后，我意识到自己正在做什么。我静了下来，开始想外衣染上墨水使我什么样的需要得不到满足。我问自己：“我责备自己‘粗心’和‘愚蠢’，是想要满足什么需要呢？”
p29.en: Fortunately, 20 minutes later, I realized what I was doing. I was quiet and began to wonder what kind of need I had to have ink on my coat. I asked myself, "What needs do I want to satisfy when I blame myself for being careless and stupid?"

p30.original: 我马上就明白了，其实我是想照顾好自己：在匆忙地回应他人的请求时，要多留意自己的需要。此时，我的心情也随即发生了变化。我不再感到恼怒、羞愧和内疚，身体也一阵轻松。我体会着损失一件新外衣及忘记戴笔帽的悲哀，以及照顾好自己的强烈愿望。
p30.en: I immediately understood that I was trying to take care of myself: when responding to others' requests in haste, pay more attention to their needs. And then my mood changed. I am no longer angry, ashamed and guilty, and my body is relaxed. I am aware of the loss of a new coat and the sadness of forgetting to wear a pen hat, as well as the desire to take care of myself.

p31.original: 接着，我开始考虑，我为了满足什么样的需要而随手把笔放入口袋中。这使我意识到，回应他人的请求对我是多么地重要。遗憾的是，为了尽量满足他人的需要，我忽视了自己的一些需要。想到这些，我并没有责备自己，而是感到对自己深深的爱——即使在我心不在焉地把笔放入口袋的时候，我也是在满足自己服务他人的渴望。
p31.en: Then I began to think about what kind of need I would put my pen in the entrance bag. This makes me realize how important it is to me to respond to others' requests. Unfortunately, I have neglected some of my own needs in order to meet the needs of others as much as possible. With that in mind, I do not blame myself, but feel deeply in love with myself — even when I put my pen in the pocket in my absence, I am fulfilling my desire to serve others.

p32.original: 这样，我做到了同时包容上述的两种需要：一方面，服务他人；另一方面，照顾好自己。我相信，在类似的情形中，只要能意识到这两方面的需要，我就能灵活地克服困难。反之，如果陷于内心的冲突，只会使情况更糟。
p32.en: In this way, I have managed to accommodate both of the above-mentioned needs: on the one hand, serving others; On the other hand, take care of yourself. I am confident that in similar situations, I will be able to overcome difficulties with flexibility, provided I am aware of the need in both areas. On the contrary, it would only make the situation worse if the conflict were confined to the heart.

p33.original: “不要做任何没有乐趣的事情！”

p34.original: 非暴力沟通的忧伤及自我宽恕可以激发我们对生命的爱。此外，我想强调的是，我们行为的动机反映了我们是否爱惜自己。当我建议“不要做任何没有乐趣的事情”时，有些人觉得我很极端，甚至精神不正常。然而，我深信，出于对生命纯洁的爱，而不是出于恐惧、内疚、羞愧、职责或义务来选择生活，是爱惜自己的重要体现。如果我们致力于满足他人及自己健康成长的需要，那么，即使艰难的工作也不乏乐趣。反之，如果我们的行为是出于义务、职责、恐惧、内疚或羞愧，那么，即使有意思的事情也会变得枯燥无味。
p34.en: The sadness of Nonviolent Communication and self-excuse can inspire our love for life. In addition, I would like to stress that the motivation for our actions reflects whether we are in love with ourselves. When I suggested “do not do anything without pleasure”, some felt that I was extreme, even mentally abnormal. I am convinced, however, that choosing life out of love for the purity of life, rather than out of fear, guilt, shame, duty or duty, is an important manifestation of love. If we are committed to meeting the needs of others and their own healthy growth, then even hard work is fun. On the contrary, if we act out of duty, duty, fear, guilt or shame, then even interesting things become boring.

p35.original: 在第二章中，我们谈到了如何使用负责任的语言来代替回避责任的语言。许多年前，有个练习给我带来了极大的快乐和欣喜，使我从此很少感到沮丧、内疚和惭愧。我将在下文中介绍这个练习，希望它有助于人们深入理解自己的人生选择，并找到快乐的生活方式。
p35.en: In chapter II, we talk about the use of responsible language as a substitute for avoiding responsibility. Many years ago, an exercise brought great joy and joy to me, which left me little sense of frustration, guilt and shame. I will present this exercise below, in the hope that it will help people to better understand their life choices and find a happy way of life.

p36.en: Replace the word “must” with the word “choice”.

p38.original: 在日常生活中，你觉得哪些事情没意思，却又认为自己不得不做？请将它们列在一张纸上。
p38.en: In everyday life, what do you think is pointless and you think you have to do it? Please place them on a piece of paper.

p39.original: 当我第一次审视自己的清单时，仅仅是它的长度就让我明白为什么我活得很不开心。我终于意识到，有许多事情，我之所以日复一日地去做，是因为我相信那是不得不做的事情。
p39.en: When I first looked at my list, its length alone made me understand why I was not happy. I finally realize that there are many things that I do day after day because I believe that that is something I have to do.

p40.original: 我清单上的第一项是“写临床报告”。我讨厌写那些报告，然而，每天我至少要折磨自己一个小时。第二项则是“开车送小孩上学”。
p40.en: The first item on my list is “Clinical Report”. I hate to write those reports, but I have to torture myself for at least an hour every day. The second one is "Drive the kids to school."

p42.original: 列好清单后，向自己坦白：你做这些事情是因为你选择了做它们，而不是因为你不得不做。在你所列的每个项目前，加上“我选择做”。
p42.en: When you're on the list, you tell yourself: You do these things because you chose to do them, not because you had to. After each item listed by you, add the words “I choose to do”.

p43.original: 当时，我对这一步骤有些抗拒。我反复强调：“写临床报告不是我的选择！我不得不做！我是一个临床心理医生。我不得不写这些报告。”
p43.en: At that time, I had some resistance to that step. I repeatedly said, "It's not my choice to write a clinical report!" I had to do it! I'm a clinical psychologist. I had to write these reports.

p45.original: 一旦承认某一行为是你的选择，就填写以下的声明来了解你为什么要那么做：“我选择做____是因为我想要____。”
p45.en: Once an act has been recognized as your choice, the following statement is written to understand why you did it: “I chose to do it because I wanted to do it.

p46.original: 起初，我怎么也想不清楚我到底为什么要写临床报告。几个月前，我已经确信，对我的病人来说，临床报告用处并不大，花那么多时间是不值得的。既然如此，为什么我一直费尽苦心准备这些报告呢？最后，我终于明白了，我选择写临床报告，是因为我想从中得到收入。于是，从35年前的那一刻起，我就再也没有写过一份临床报告。想到自己少写了无数的临床报告，我的快乐真是无法形容！当认识到钱是我的主要动机时，我马上就想到我可以用别的方式来获得收入；而事实上，我宁可在垃圾箱中觅食，也不愿再写一份临床报告。
p46.en: At first, I couldn't figure out why I had to write a clinical report. A few months ago, I was convinced that clinical reports were not very useful to my patients and that it was not worth the time spent. Then why have I been working so hard to prepare these reports? Finally, I finally understood that I chose to write a clinical report because I wanted to get paid for it. So, from the moment I was 35 years ago, I never wrote a clinical report. I can't describe my happiness when I think I've done so many less clinical reports! When I realized that money was my main motivation, I immediately realized that I could get my income in another way; And in fact, I'd rather eat in a dumpster than write another clinical report.

p47.original: 我清单上的第二项是开车送孩子上学。当我琢磨自己为何要这么做时，我发现，我很欣赏我的孩子从他们现在的学校得到的教育。虽然他们可以步行到附近的学校上学，但他们所在的学校提供的教育更符合我的价值观。想到这一点，在开车送孩子上学时，我的感受就不一样了。在这以前，我会说：“倒霉！今天又不得不开车送孩子上学。”而在这之后，我理解自己为什么要这么做——那是为了孩子们能够得到我所看重的教育。当然，有的时候，在路上我需要提醒自己两三次开车送孩子上学的意义。
p47.en: The second thing on my list is to drive the kids to school. When I wondered why I wanted to do it, I found out that I appreciated the education my children received from their present schools. While they can walk to nearby schools, the education they provide is more in line with my values. I thought about it, and I felt differently when I drove my kids to school. Before that, I'd say, "Damn it! Today we have to drive our children to school. And after that, I understand why I did it — it was so that the children could get the education that I valued. Sometimes, of course, on the way I need to remind myself of the significance of driving my children to school two or three times.

p48.original: 深入理解我们行为的动机
p48.en: To understand the motives of our actions.

p49.original: 你在思考“我选择做____是因为我想____”这个问题时，也许会像我考虑开车送小孩上学时那样，发现自己行为背后的价值取向——你在生活中看重什么。我确信，一旦意识到我们的行为所服务的需要，即使工作很艰苦、富有挑战性乃至举步维艰，我们也会从中得到乐趣。
p49.en: When you think about “I choose to do it because I want to do it”, you might find the value behind my behavior, as I did when I thought about driving my kids to school — what you value in life. I am sure that, once we realize the needs that our actions serve, we will enjoy even the hard, challenging and even the hard work.

p50.original: 然而，你也许会发现，清单上的一些行为是出于下列的一种或多种动机：
p50.en: However, you may find that some of the listed acts are motivated by one or more of the following:

p52.original: 钱是社会回报一个人的主要形式。如果我们的行动是为了得到报酬，我们付出的代价是失去生活的乐趣；反之，如果我们的行动只是出于对生命的爱，快乐将会伴随着我们。在非暴力沟通中，钱并不被认为是一种“需要”；它只是被用来满足某种需要的无数种策略中的一种。
p52.en: Money is the main form of social reward for a person. If we act to get paid, we pay the price of losing the pleasure of life; On the contrary, happiness will accompany us if our actions are motivated only by love for life. In Nonviolent Communication, money is not considered a “need”; It is only one of the countless strategies used to meet a certain need.

p54.original: 像钱一样，来自他人的赞同也是一种回报。受社会化的影响，我们渴望得到奖励。上学时，学校使用外在的手段来激励我们学习。在家里，做一个好男孩或好女孩，我们就会得到礼物；反之，如果大人认为我们调皮捣蛋，我们就会受罚。于是，等我们长大成人，我们误以为生活的目的就是为了获得回报。我们迫切地希望得到人们的微笑，听到一点鼓励，盼着人们夸我们是“好人”“好家长”“好市民”“好员工”以及“好朋友”等等。为了讨人喜欢，我们努力迎合他人；为了避免招人嫌恶，我们不做那些不受人欢迎的事情。
p54.en: Like money, consent from others is a reward. We are eager to be rewarded by the influence of socialization. When we go to school, schools use external means to motivate us to study. At home, be a good boy or a good girl and we get a gift; On the other hand, if adults think we're naughty, we'll be punished. So, when we grow up, we think that the purpose of our lives is to get paid. We are eager to be smiled, to hear a little encouragement, to be praised as “good people”, “good parents”, “good citizens”, “good people”, “good friends”, etc. We try to be nice to others; We do not do things that are unpopular in order to avoid being offensive.

p55.original: 于是，为了博得他人的喜爱，我们费尽心思、委曲求全。这是很可悲的。实际上，如果我们的行为只是出于对生命的爱，人们自然会心存感激。他们的感激也是在给我们确认：我们的行为有益于他们的生活。一旦如愿活出对生命的爱，我们所体会到的欢乐是他人的赞同永远无法给予的。
p55.en: And so, in order to get the love of others, we spent all our time trying to get the love of others. It's sad. Indeed, if we act out of love for life, it is natural to be grateful. Their gratitude is also confirming to us that our actions are beneficial to their lives. Once the love for life is alive as desired, the joy that we experience is something that others can never give.

p57.original: 有些人缴纳个人所得税主要是为了免受惩罚。这使他们对每年度例行的纳税产生了抵触情绪。然而，想起小时候我父亲及祖父对纳税的态度，感到真是今非昔比。他们从俄罗斯移民到美国，热衷于支持一个他们认为比沙皇更能保护人民利益的政府。想到许多人的福利有赖于他们的纳税，每次将支票寄给美国政府时，他们都无比地喜悦。
p57.en: Some pay personal income taxes primarily to avoid punishment. This creates resistance to routine annual tax payments. However, it is not true that my father's and grandfather's attitude towards taxation was similar when I was a child. They emigrated from Russia to the United States and were keen to support a Government that they believed was better able to protect the interests of the people than the tsar. It is with great joy to think that the welfare of many depends on their taxation, and every time they send a cheque to the United States Government.

p59.original: 我们知道，如果不做某些事情，我们就会责备自己。我们认为不做那些事情是不对的、愚蠢的。可是，如果为了体面而循规蹈矩，我们最终难免会感到厌烦。
p59.en: We know that if we do not do something, we will blame ourselves. We think it's wrong not to do those things. It's stupid. But if we behave with dignity, we will eventually be bored.

p61.original: 在另外一些情形，我们也许会想：“如果我不做这件事，别人会感到失望。”此时，我们担心无法满足他人的期待。同样一件事情，不同的目的会给我们带来截然不同的感受。如果为了避免内疚，我们将活得可怜兮兮；如果为了活出对他人的爱，我们的生活将充满乐趣。
p61.en: In other cases, we might think, “If I don't do this, others will be disappointed. At this time, we fear that we will not be able to meet the expectations of others. The same thing, different ends bring us a very different feeling. If we don't feel guilty, we'll live miserablely; If we live to love others, our lives will be full of joy.

p62.en: 6) for the purpose of discharging their duties

p63.original: 使用“应该”“不得不”“应当”“必须”“不能”“被迫”这样的词语，意味着我们受到内疚、职责或义务的逼迫，感到自己无可奈何。我确信，一旦生命的需要被忽视，我们的行动对社会来说极具危险，对个人来说则极为不幸。
p63.en: The use of the words “shall” “must” “must” “must” “can not” means that we feel compelled by guilt, duty or obligation to feel helpless. I am convinced that, once the need for life is ignored, our actions are extremely dangerous for society and extremely unfortunate for individuals.

p64.original: 在第二章中，我们看到“行政命令”（Amtssprache）这一概念的恶果：艾希曼及其同事使数以万计的人丧命，却不认为负有任何的个人责任。当我们认为自己无可奈何时，我们不再是生活的主人，而是沦为了机器。
p64.en: In chapter II, we see the negative consequences of the concept of “administrative order” (Amtsprache): Eichmann and his colleagues have killed tens of thousands of people without considering that they have any personal responsibility. When we feel we have no choice, we are no longer the masters of life, but the machines.

p65.original: 在仔细思考清单上所列的各项事情后，你也许会像我选择放弃写临床报告那样，决定不做某些事情。即使这听起来似乎很激进，但我们只做有乐趣的事情是可能的。我相信，我们越是投入服务生命的乐趣中——服务生命是唯一的目的，我们也就越爱自己。
p65.en: You may decide not to do something, as I have chosen to give up writing clinical reports, after careful reflection on the items on the list. Even if that sounds radical, it is possible that we only do things that are fun. I believe that the more we are committed to the pleasure of serving life — the more we love ourselves for the sole purpose.

p67.original: 非暴力沟通最重要的应用也许在于培育对自己的爱。当我们的表现不完美时，我们可以通过体会忧伤和自我宽恕，来看清个人成长的方向，以及避免自我惩罚。评价自己的行为时，我们专注于尚未满足的需要；这样，我们就不再依赖羞愧、内疚、恼怒或沮丧的心理来寻求改变，而让爱主导我们的学习和成长。
p67.en: Perhaps the most important application of Nonviolent Communication is to nurture love for oneself. When our performance is not perfect, we can see the direction of individual growth and avoid self-punitiveness by feeling sorrow and self-excusing. In evaluating our behaviour, we focus on unmet needs; In this way, we will no longer rely on shame, guilt, anger or frustration to seek change, leaving love to lead our learning and growth.

p68.original: 同时，在日常生活中，我们主动根据需要和价值观来选择生活。我们的行为不再是为了履行职责、获得回报、逃避惩罚或避免感到内疚和羞愧。通过深入理解我们行为的动机，并用“选择做”来取代“不得不”，我们的生活将变得和谐并充满欢乐。
p68.en: At the same time, in our daily lives, we choose our lives on the basis of needs and values. Our actions are no longer aimed at discharging our duties, obtaining rewards, escaping punishment or avoiding guilt and shame. By understanding in depth the motives of our actions and replacing “must” with “choice to do”, our lives will become harmonious and full of joy.
